{{Quote|I'm afraid there's no place on Esseles that's prepared to heal a Jedi.''"<br />"''Wait! There's a Jedi chapter house on the planet Rhinnal. Rhinnal is famous for its expertise in medicine and it's in the Darpa Sector. We can get Master Adi there in no time!|Noro Zak and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Episode Adv 1">''[[Episode I Adventures 1: Search for the Lost Jedi]]''</ref>}}
'''Rhinnal''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Star system/Legends|star system]] of the [[Rhinnal system/Legends|same name]] in the [[Darpa sector/Legends|Darpa sector]] of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. [[Orbit/Legends|Orbited]] by two [[Moon/Legends|moons]] and located in the [[Ringali Shell]], the region of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] along the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] near the [[Ringali Nebula/Legends|Ringali Nebula]], Rhinnal possessed almost no axial tilt and a near-circular orbit, giving the planet very little seasonal variations. Encased in a planet-wide ice age tens of thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] collapse, Rhinnal had begun to thaw by the [[Time/Legends|time]] it was one of the [[Core Founder/Legends|Core Founders]] of the Republic in [[25,053 BBY]], having been settled by [[Human/Legends|Humans]] from the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Notron]]. A colony of nearby [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]] for much of its history, Rhinnal soon gained a reputation as a medical wonderworld, with a [[Jedi chapter house (Rhinnal)|Jedi chapter house]] and the [[Rhinnal State Medical Academy]] in the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Rhire]] producing some of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] best [[Doctor/Legends|doctors]].

Renowned for its beauty and pristine environment, Rhinnal also developed a textile industry in addition to its pharmaceutical and [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]] industry, and the native Rhinnalians were known for their fierce loyalty to their clans. Freed from Esseles' control with the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Rhinnal eventually overthrew its [[Governor/Legends|governor]] [[Phadreas Kole]] in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]] and joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], supplying its doctors and medical experts to help halt crises such as the outbreak of the [[Krytos virus]] and the [[Death Seed]] plague. Rhinnal willingly accepted thousands of [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|war]] with the [[Extragalactic/Legends|extragalactic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Species/Legends|species]], though [[Transport/Legends|transports]] full of some of those same refugees were used as ammunition against the [[Planetary shield/Legends|shields]] of the capital of Notron, since renamed to Coruscant, by the Yuuzhan Vong during their [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|capture]] of the planet.

==Description==
{{Quote|It was many years ago, during the expansion of the Jedi chapter house. Building materials had to be delivered because so much of the planet's surface was still covered by ice.''"<br />"''You'll find Rhinnal hasn't changed much. Terraforming has created new forests, but it's still colder than a mynock's wingtips.|Qui-Gon Jinn and Bama Vook|<ref name="Episode Adv 3">''[[Episode I Adventures 3: The Fury of Darth Maul]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Farorbitringaliee0.jpg|thumb|left|310px|The Ringali Shell, with Rhinnal as the second from the right]]
The fourth [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in orbit around the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Rhinnal (star)|Rhinnal]] in the [[Rhinnal system/Legends|Rhinnal system]],<ref name="Core Worlds" /> Rhinnal was located in the region of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] known as the [[Ringali Shell]], a string of [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] along the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]] that were near the violet-[[Color/Legends|colored]] [[Ringali Nebula/Legends|Ringali Nebula]] and whose night skies were lit up by the same [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]].<ref name="Into the Core" /> Situated along the Perlemian between the planets [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]] and [[Ralltiir/Legends|Ralltiir]], Rhinnal was located in the [[Darpa sector/Legends|Darpa sector]]<ref name="Core Worlds" /> in the [[Arrowhead]], the Core Worlds portion of the galactic region known as [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]],<ref name="Region" /> and it was orbited by two [[Moon/Legends|moons]]. The terrestrial planet's diameter was 12,900 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]], and it had a 27-[[Standard hour/Legends|hour]] [[Standard day/Legends|day]] and a 357-day [[Standard year/Legends|year]], with standard gravity, a breathable [[Atmosphere/Legends|Type I atmosphere]], and a climate that ranged from chilly temperate to arctic. Tens of thousands of years before the fall of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Rhinnal was experiencing a planet-wide ice age that slowly faded over the course of [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], with the glaciers exposing the planet's landmasses and leaving behind [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]], valleys, and crystal-clear lakes as they retreated.<ref name="Core Worlds" />

Rhinnal's rocky continents were marked by the narrow finger-like bays that split the high cliffs along their coasts, giving the shorelines a fringed appearance when viewed from above. The planet experienced virtually no axial tilt and had a particularly circular orbit, resulting in very insignificant seasonal variations, and much of the planet was covered by glaciers, tundras, and frozen rivers. The equatorial regions of Rhinnal were home to mossy slopes and evergeen forests, and the planet's ambient temperature was significantly lower than other worlds to the point where every visitor was advised to bring a jacket. Snow fell frequently during the night on Rhinnal, but the reduced amounts near the equator typically melted by morning. Rhinnal was also prone to electromagnetic storms that swept across the equatorial regions several times a year, and engineers had begun to use [[Terraforming/Legends|terraforming]] to increase the planet's self-sufficiency by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], since all attempts to farm share crops on any part of the planet never succeeded. As a result, the planet imported raw materials and [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]] from other worlds. The wooly [[gabal]], the rare [[snow falcon]], the [[Limb/Legends|limbed]] [[Fish/Legends|fish]] known as [[firehead]]s, and the fireheads' predators, the [[tenticulon]]s, were among the creatures native to the world.<ref name="Core Worlds" />

==History==
===Early history===
{{Quote|The Jedi enclave on Rhinnal has been destroyed, along with the Republic patrol frigate ''Toron Voq''.|Satele Shan|<ref name="Red Reaper" />}}
Tens of thousands of years before the rise of the Galactic Empire, Rhinnal reached the end of a planetary ice age;<ref name="Core Worlds" /> by the time [[Sleeper ship/Legends|sleeper ships]] carrying [[Human/Legends|Human]] colonists from the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Notron]] reached the Ringali Shell sometime after [[27,000 BBY/Legends|27,000 BBY]],<ref name="Atlas" /> the planet's glaciers had retreated from the equatorial regions, leaving Rhinnal habitable. Sometime before the Galactic Republic's founding in [[25,053 BBY]], a [[Dellaltian warship|warship]] from the planet [[Dellalt/Legends|Dellalt]] crashed near the planet's southern pole, and it became buried in the ice over the following millennia.<ref name="Core Worlds" /> Rhinnal was one of the [[Core Founder/Legends|Core Founders]] of the Republic,<ref name="Atlas" /> but for much of the planet's history, it was a colony of the [[Esselian Empire]] and ruled by a [[Governor/Legends|governor]] from its neighbor Esseles.<ref name="Far Orbit">''[[The Far Orbit Project]]''</ref>

[[File:Red_Reaper.png|thumb|right|300px|The ''Red Reaper'', which attacked Rhinnal during the Cold War]]
When Rhinnal's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Rhire]] was still only a supply outpost on the banks of the [[Frieste River]] for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] explorers heading out along the Perlemian, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] established a [[Jedi chapter house (Rhinnal)|chapter house]] to the west of the city, a simple, spired structure that could hold almost a hundred patients.<ref name="Core Worlds" /> By the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], Rhinnal's native snow falcon was on the verge of extinction, and hunting the birds was a crime that was punishable with life imprisonment.<ref name="Poaching">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Underworld Trading|Poaching}}</ref> The planet also had a thriving textile industry by that point, though a [[Unidentified textile transport|transport]] carrying [[Ayelixe Fabrico/Legends|Ayelixe Fabrico]] textiles once exploded in the atmosphere over the planet and scattered its cargo for kilometers.<ref name="Fleeced">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Scavenging|Fleeced}}</ref>

During the Cold War, the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Ikoral]] returned to the larger [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] and embarked on a series of attacks against both the Empire and the Republic, viewing neither of the governments as acceptable due to his extreme belief that the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith pureblood]] [[Species/Legends|species]] was superior. Ikoral's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the ''[[Red Reaper]]'', [[Attack on Rhinnal|attacked]] the planet and destroyed the chapter house on Rhinnal. The enclave's destruction was sensed by [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Satele Shan]] all the way on the planet [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], and the Republic patrol [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]] ''[[Toron Voq]]'' was destroyed by the ''Red Reaper'' when it was sent to investigate Rhinnal.<ref name="Red Reaper" />

===Twilight of the Republic===
The Jedi chapter house was later rebuilt, and several [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], it was expanded; [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] was one of the Jedi who delivered building materials to the chapter house because none could be procured from Rhinnal's ice-covered surface.<ref name="Episode Adv 3" /> The [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Zahara Cody]] was one of many who attended the [[Rhinnal State Medical Academy]] in Rhire,<ref name="Death Troopers">''[[Death Troopers]]''</ref> and the diagnostic database of the [[2-1B surgical droid/Legends|2-1B surgical droid]] model was programmed by a team of surgical experts<ref name="NEGD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> from the Academy.<ref name="Death Troopers" />

[[File:Rhire.png|thumb|left|320px|A map of Rhire around the time of the Clone Wars]]
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="EpIAdv">The first four installments of the ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Adventures]]'' series form a continuous story that is set prior to the events of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] possesses the [[Scimitar/Legends|''Scimitar'']] during the series, and ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates both his acquisition of the ship and the events of ''The Phantom Menance'' to 32 BBY, thus placing the events of the first four ''Episode I Adventures'' books in 32 BBY as well.</ref> the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] was grievously injured on Esseles, and the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Vel Ardox]] and [[Noro Zak]] brought Gallia to Rhinnal for treatment.<ref name="Episode Adv 1" /> The Knights arrived at Rhinnal just after an electromagnetic storm had knocked out Rhire's power grid and all of the planet's communications satellites, preventing the [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] from making contact with Rhinnal over any of the standard channels, so his Master Qui-Gon Jinn decided to travel to Rhinnal to investigate. The [[Talz/Legends|Talz]] pilot [[Bama Vook]] brought the pair to the Rhinnal system, but when the chapter house did not respond to their hails, the two Jedi descended to the complex. However, when they learned of the storm, the two were also prevented from leaving, as another storm was due in three hours.<ref name="Episode Adv 3" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="CWdate">[[HoloNet News Vol. 531 47|''HoloNet News Vol. 531'' #47]] is dated to "13:3:14," which is a [[Great ReSynchronization]] date corresponding to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], per the reasoning [[:Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> the [[Allied Tion Historical Society]]'s "[[Cradle of the Galaxy]]" exhibit of [[Pre-Republic era|pre-Republic]] artifacts began a tour of the Core Worlds on 13:4:1 on Ralltiir, and it arrived on Rhinnal five [[Standard month/Legends|months]] later on 13:9:1. The exhibit was showcased in the [[Rhire Concourse of Humanity and History]] for five months before it moved on to Esseles on 14:2:3. Two weeks after the tour's announcement on 13:3:14,<ref name="Xim">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|47|life/13314_4.html|New Xim Exhibit to Tour}}</ref> the State Medical Academy released their findings on the status of air pollution in the middle-class districts of the galactic capital of Coruscant,<ref name="Study">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49|life/13328_4.html|Study: Pollution Standards Still Endanger Many}}</ref> and two months later, the Academy's staff were among those health officials who criticized the high-gravity planet of [[Columus/Legends|Columus's]] marketing campaign toward the severely overweight.<ref name="Healthy">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|56|life/13516_1.html|Healthy Vacation Claims Disputed}}</ref>

===The Empire and beyond===
{{Quote|With all those refugee convoys disappearing from Ralltiir and Rhinnal, this is more than just quiet.|Jedi Master [[Mara Jade Skywalker]], during the Yuuzhan Vong War|<ref name="Star by Star">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>}}
The Clone Wars ran from 22 BBY to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], and at their end, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] reformed the Republic into the Galactic Empire and [[Order 66/Legends|eradicated]] the Jedi Order. However, because of the planet's reputation, the chapter house on Rhinnal was spared from destruction unlike the other chapter houses across the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], and it was taken over by Rhinnal's doctors.<ref name="Core Worlds" /> Under the Empire, Rhinnal was granted marginal independence, as the Esselian Empire had collapsed shortly before the Clone Wars due to financial difficulties. The [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of the Darpa sector, [[Jander Graffe]], reined in Esseles' power and overturned Rhinnal's classification as an Esselian colony, installing [[Phadreas Kole]] as an Imperial governor.<ref name="Core Worlds" /> The Empire established the [[Imperial Merchant Galactic Academy]], a civilian auxiliary of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy's]] academy system, on Rhinnal, and its students specialized in military transportation and logistics.<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], medical experts from Rhinnal were sent to study the outbreak of the dangerous [[Candorian plague/Legends|Candorian plague]] on the planet [[Dentaal/Legends|Dentaal]].<ref name="GNN" />

[[File:RhinnalFarOrbit.png|thumb|right|300px|A medical facility on Rhinnal]]
Kole was largely off-hands in his leadership, leading [[Rhinnalian]] opposition to the Empire to be muted until [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. six months after the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[Death/Legends|killed]] Palpatine at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the newly-formed [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|captured]] the nearby planet of [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]], rattling Rhinnal's citizens. An organized resistance movement soon formed and succeeded in overthrowing Kole in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], and the planet became a valued member of the New Republic, sending its best doctors to combat the virulent [[Krytos virus]] that was ravaging Coruscant at the time.<ref name="Core Worlds" /> [[13 ABY/Legends|Six years later]],<ref name="Planet of Twilight">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref> they once again contributed their medical aid when the [[Death Seed]] plague threatened to spread across the galaxy, and when the extra-galactic [[Yuuzhan Vong]] species [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invaded]] the galaxy in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], Rhinnal took in thousands of [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="Core Worlds" />

After the planet received ten thousand refugees from the planet [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]], Governor-General [[Amer Tariq]] was forced to reroute two thousand more to the [[Ruan system/Legends|Ruan system]], and he turned down [[Ambassador/Legends|Ambassador]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo's]] request to land more refugees, but sent her in the direction of the planet [[Ruan]].<ref name="Agents">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref> The Yuuzhan Vong began to capture refugees around Rhinnal during the months before their [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|attack]] on Coruscant<ref name="Star by Star" /> in [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]'' to [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]].</ref> during which they used transports carrying refugees to bombard the capital's [[Planetary shield/Legends|shields]].<ref name="Star by Star" /> Rhinnal's chapter house was among several Jedi facilities discussed in a section on [[Force healing/Legends|Force healing]] in the compendium ''[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force]]'', which written by the Jedi Master [[Tionne Solusar]] in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]].<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|Rhinnal cannot possibly accept additional refugees at this time, even on a temporary basis.''"<br />"''Amer, if this is about funds&hellip;''"<br />"''Don't confuse Rhinnal with Ralltiir, my dear. It's simply that the ten thousand refugees we received from Ord Mantell have strained our resources to the breaking point.|Amer Tariq and Leia Organa Solo|<ref name="Agents" />}}
Rhinnalians, as the inhabitants of Rhinnal were known, were primarily Human, with Humans making up 92% of the population of 55 million, and the planet's inhabitants spoke [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. The planet's cities were centers of healing and business, producing doctors of great skill and renown, and Rhinnal was also a player in the textile industry, though the planet's Rhinnalian rugs were considered more of a luxury due to their high cost.<ref name="Core Worlds" /> The planet had a reputation among the Core Worlds of having an atmosphere of exclusivity, one that was reflected in manners, clothing, and decor, and Rhinnalians were considered experts in passive aggression, routinely snubbing off-worlders and [[Alien/Legends|aliens]]. Rhinnalian industry was also centered on [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]] and pharmaceuticals in addition to their medical expertise.<ref name="Far Orbit" />

Rhinnalians were markedly different from other Core Worlders, as they were fiercely loyal to their ethnic clans, and major governmental decisions were made by the heads of those clans. Rhinnalians were also fond of elaborate ceremonies; a total of eighty-four days of the planet's calendar were set aside for celebrations and holidays. Native Rhinnalians typically wore colorful, patterned clothing that had been hand-woven from the wool of the gabal. Rhinnal's medical community was more cosmopolitan, with most graduates of the Medical Academy being offworlders.<ref name="Core Worlds" /> Rhinnalian culture valued honor and style, traits that inspired their fascination with ceremony.<ref name="Hero">''[[Heroes & Rogues]]''</ref>

==Locations==
{{Quote|I tried sending a message to the Jedi chapter house on Rhinnal to check on Adi Gallia's condition. There's no response. I'm only getting static. It might just be subspace interference.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Episode Adv 2">''[[Episode I Adventures 2: The Bartokk Assassins]]''</ref>}}
[[File:ZirfanGlacier.jpg|thumb|left|310px|The city of Rhire, across the Frieste]]
As much of the planet was still covered by glaciers, the inhabitants of Rhinnal mostly inhabited the world's more temperate equatorial regions. Rhinnal's capital city of Rhire, with over seven million inhabitants, lay along the north banks of the Frieste River in the southern fringes of the equatorial band, and it was home to both the Jedi chapter house and the Rhinnal State Medical Academy. Street traffic in the city was largely light, as most of the residents used the underground [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] network known as the [[Circulation Network]] to get around Rhire, and hydroelectric energy plants along the banks of the Frieste powered the city.<ref name="Core Worlds" />

The State Medical Academy covered many square kilometers in the heart of Rhire, with three working hospitals and dozens of classrooms, clinics, and laboratories. The three hospitals each catered to a different group; one specialized in treating Humans, a second [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] aliens, and a third treated aliens whose biology was radically different than humanoids. To the north of Rhire was the [[Zirfan glacier]] and the [[Sennes Mountains]], where native Rhinnalian clans hunted the wild gabals for their wool and schools of fireheads lived in the ice of the glacier. [[V-Fin submersible icebreaker|V-Fin submersible ice breakers]] were frequently used by recreational tourists to tour the planet's oceans and poles, though cheaper submersibles were used when exploring the less dangerous riverbeds and submerged caves of Rhinnal's waterways. The clan village of [[Austogie]] was located to the south of Rhire in the territory of the [[Kieger clan]].<ref name="Core Worlds" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Adventures3.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Rhinnal first appeared in ''The Fury of Darth Maul''.]]
Rhinnal was first mentioned in the "[[Galaxywide NewsNets]]" segment written by [[Paul Sudlow]] that appeared in the [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 5|fifth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'', a magazine published by [[West End Games]] in [[February]] [[1995]].<ref name="GNN">{{JournalCite|5|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> It was first pictured in the ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' supplement ''[[The Far Orbit Project]]'', which was written by [[Timothy S. O'Brien]] and published in [[1998]],<ref name="Far Orbit" /> and went on to make its first full appearance in ''[[Episode I Adventures 3: The Fury of Darth Maul]]'', a children's adventure book written by [[Ryder Windham]] in [[1999]].<ref name="Episode Adv 3" />

The [[2003]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' sourcebook ''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]'' erroneously used its illustration of Rhinnal to also depict the planet Ralltiir,<ref name="Core Worlds" /> an error that was repeated in ''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]'' published in [[2008]] for use with the ''Star Wars Roleplaying Game''.<ref name="TFU">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Rhinnal was one of several planets that were planned to appear in but were ultimately cut from the [[2006]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', though images of the planet remained in the game's files.<ref name="Empire at War">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed Rhinnal in grid square L-9.<ref name="Atlas" />
